note: Recast from the genus-level monograph description of Roonwal & Chhotani (1989), in English, which is itself recast from the original description of Akhtar 1974; the alate and the soldier are described and measured, the pseudoworker is not described there. Type locality Pasni, Balochistan, Pakistan.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head reddish brown, postclypeus paler; anteclypeus white; antennae pale brown; pronotum as dark as the head; labrum and legs pale brown with a reddish tinge; wings nearly white, the costa pale brown; abdominal tergites reddish brown. Head with a few short hairs and scattered long setae; labrum with a row of setae near the apex and a few hairs in the middle; pronotum with short hairs and long setae on the margins and surface; wings with a few hairs along the costal margin. Head semicircular; length to the mandibular base 0.98—1.11, width 1.18—1.25 mm; the sides behind the compound eyes nearly parallel; the long arm of the Y suture slightly visible. Compound eyes broadly oval, long diameter 0.23—0.26, short diameter 0.21—0.24 mm. Ocelli oval, length 0.07—0.09 mm, touching the compound eye but separated from its lower margin by about their diameter. Antenna 15—16 segments; segment 2 slightly longer than segment 3, segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 3 and about as long as segment 5. Anteclypeus trapezoidal. Labrum dome-shaped, wider than long; sides weakly convex; anterior margin nearly straight in the middle. Mandibles as in the genus. Pronotum wider than the head; maximum width 1.29—1.47, maximum length 0.70—0.76 mm; anterior margin shallowly concave; sides weakly convex; posterior margin incurved in the middle. The main veins of the forewing arise independently at the wing suture; media less sclerotised than the radial sector and closer to the radial sector than to the cubitus. Apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3, the middle tibia with a conspicuous spine slightly above the spur; tarsi 4-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale reddish brown, paler posteriorly; labrum pale brown with a reddish tinge; mandibles reddish brown at the base, dark brown to black apically; antennae pale brown; pronotum slightly paler than the head; legs and abdomen yellowish brown. Head sparsely hairy; anterior margin of the labrum with a few setae, and the surface also; anterior third of the postmentum with a few long setae, the posterior half with a few short hairs; pronotum with short hairs and long setae on the margins and surface. Head long, rectangular; length to the mandibular base 1.80—3.19, width 1.28—1.71 mm; sides nearly straight; posterior margin nearly straight; Y suture present; frons weakly sloping anteriorly, the sides below the antennal carinae distinctly rugose. Compound eyes oval, large, margins indistinct. Antenna 13—15 segments; segments 2 and 3 nearly equal in length; segment 4 the shortest. Labrum dome-shaped, wider than long, sides weakly convex. Mandibles long and stout, the base conspicuously swollen; left mandible length 1.12—1.51 mm; left mandible with 5 marginal teeth, the 1st and 2nd well developed, the 3rd, 4th and 5th weak; right mandible with 2 marginal teeth. Postmentum long, club-shaped, widest anteriorly, narrowest below the middle; length 1.22—2.48, maximum width 0.67—0.91, minimum width 0.20—0.28 mm. Pronotum wider than the head; maximum width 1.25—2.10, maximum length 0.70—1.12 mm; anterior margin deeply concave; sides weakly convex; posterior margin distinctly incurved in the middle. Apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3, the outer side of the middle tibia with a large spine above the apical spur; tarsi 4-segmented.
